> ⚠️ Uses FOR UPDATE row locks on both user_profiles and the (uid,'lead_gen') entitlements row inside one transaction to close a TOCTOU race against a concurrent webhook. Reuses an existing unexpired nonce rather than always inserting a new one (idempotent within the 15-minute window). Distinct 400 codes route already-entitled, past_due (to the portal) and deletion-pending users differently instead of a generic error. | MEASURED 2026-09-15: No Stripe call at all — this route only mints the nonce; the Stripe Checkout Session is created downstream by /api/subscribe/exchange. resolveCheckoutBaseUrl() (:37-48) THROWS in non-production when SUBSCRIBE_CHECKOUT_BASE_URL is unset; that throw is raised at :80 inside the try and lands on the generic 500 at :237. CENSUS AGREEMENT: matches (reads user_profiles + entitlements; writes subscribe_nonces) — plus an unlisted READ of subscribe_nonces at :146, which the census's read list omits. | Idempotency: Guarded and safe to repeat within the nonce window: a still-unexpired nonce for the same user is SELECTed FOR UPDATE and reused instead of inserting a new row (:146-156), so a double-tapped CTA returns the same URL and does not pollute the table. The FOR UPDATE at :151 serialises concurrent same-user calls. The INSERT (:164) is backstopped by the `nonce` PRIMARY KEY (migrations/114:88). | Caching: none observed — no Cache-Control header, no revalidate/dynamic export (full file read :1-241) | Entitlement posture: getEntitlementStatusForUpdate(client, uid, DEFAULT_PRODUCT) at src/app/api/subscribe/session/route.ts:119 -> `SELECT status, trial_started_at FROM entitlements WHERE user_id = $1 AND product = $2 FOR UPDATE` (src/lib/entitlements/index.ts:116). Three gates on the result: DELETION_BLOCKED_STATUSES {'cancelled_pending_deletion'} :68/:121-126; PORTAL_ROUTED_STATUSES {'past_due'} :61/:127-129; ALREADY_ENTITLED_STATUSES {'active','admin_managed'} :53/:130-132. Plus an account-level `account_deleted_at` gate on the row-locked user_profiles read at :102-118. | Other guards / classification: Nonce MINTING side of the single-use contract: an unexpired nonce is reused under FOR UPDATE (:146-156) rather than churning new rows; otherwise a fresh randomUUID() is inserted (:158,:164-167). No signature/replay guard (this route is session-authenticated). | Locking tests: src/tests/subscribe-portal-session.infra.test.ts, src/tests/subscribe-session.infra.test.ts, src/tests/subscribe-session.security.test.ts.

###### `C-038` `contract_webhooks_stripe`

**Programme.** `C-038` · scope `platform_shared` · feature `F12` · build order 3122 · batch **UNRESEARCHED** · review `unreviewed` — Used by both products and owned by neither.

**What it is.** Receives payment-status events directly from the payment provider — checkout completed, subscription created, updated or cancelled, invoice paid or failed — and updates the corresponding user's paid-access status. This is the mechanism that actually turns a subscriber's access on or off after billing is processed.

**What it reads and writes.** It reads 3 tables — `entitlements`, `user_profiles` and `logic_variables` and writes `stripe_webhook_events` and `entitlements`. Its response shape is **unmeasured** as a pick-by-name whitelist — it passes rows through, spreads a row into a computed object, or assembles the payload dynamically, so there is no single list naming what leaves the server. **Nothing in this repository calls it.** That is the state this registry exists to make visible, not a claim that it is dead — a caller could be a bookmark, an external system, or a path built from variables.

**Under Spec 126.** Becomes a **CONTRACT descriptor** of archetype `WEBHOOK`. It declares its signature verification, its closed `events[]` set, its replay guard, its ordering watermark and its behaviour on an unknown event. Its `consumers[]` is the field that matters most here: today it is empty, and the orphan panel renders that as a red row rather than leaving it to be discovered years later.

> ⚠️ Also cites docs/specs/00-architecture/116_multi_product_architecture.md §4. Verifies the Stripe-Signature header against STRIPE_WEBHOOK_SECRET before trusting any payload and enforces a 1MB body cap as a DoS guard on this public route. The dedup INSERT into stripe_webhook_events and the entitlements upsert run in one transaction so a provider retry cannot double-apply an event. The response body is the provider-required { received: true } shape, not the app's standard envelope. ###### `S-043` `overlay_paywall`

**Programme.** `S-043` · scope `platform_shared` · feature `F12` · build order 3123 · batch **UNRESEARCHED** · review `unreviewed` — The subscription and Stripe hand-off, which resolves an entitlement per PRODUCT — so it serves both and belongs to neither.

**⚠️ Cross-product leakage (1).** Renders trial copy from `user_profiles.lead_views_count` — a lead-gen counter — on a paywall that also stands in front of the parcel product. The counter is structurally 0 (its only writer has no caller), so every trial user sees the zero-state copy regardless of which product they came from. → `needs-ruling` (`mobile/src/components/paywall/PaywallScreen.tsx:153`, `src/app/api/leads/view/route.ts:100-114`, `src/features/leads/api/useLeadView.ts:77`)

**❓ Product question(s) (1).** Should the trial paywall tell a parcel-tool user how many LEADS they have viewed? The copy is lead-gen framing on a gate that also stands in front of the parcel product. — see §2.9.

**What it is.** The full-screen message a user meets when their free trial has run out. It tells them how many jobs they viewed during the trial and offers a button that opens a checkout page in a browser. They can also dismiss it and keep browsing with everything blurred out. If they have already paid and nothing has changed, a link appears after a minute to re-check their status.

**What it reads and writes.** It reads nothing from the database directly. Every value arrives through one contract: `/api/subscribe/session`. Behind that contract, the data comes from `entitlements` and `user_profiles`, and writes land on `subscribe_nonces`. It also holds client-side state in `paywallStore`, which is the part a server-driven projection has to absorb or justify.

**Under Spec 126.** **REBUILD** — it holds Layer-3 state (`paywallStore`) and drives writes, so a client decision has to be re-homed on the server before the projection can be honest. It renders through the GATE renderer (a `statuses_handled[]` that must cover every value of the closed set it gates on), reading by reference: `/api/subscribe/session`. Its `owns.components[]` declares `mobile/src/components/paywall/PaywallScreen.tsx`.

**What it is.** A plain full-screen spinner shown in the moment before the app knows whether the user's subscription is still valid. Its whole job is to make sure the upgrade screen never flashes up at someone who is actually a paying customer. It is also reused when the app is briefly unsure which user's data it is holding.

**What it reads and writes.** This surface reaches **no API contract at all** — every value it shows is local, passed in as a prop, or read from the device. It holds no client-side store, so there is no local copy of server state to keep in sync. It emits **no analytics event**, so nothing it does is currently countable.

It renders through the GATE renderer (a `statuses_handled[]` that must cover every value of the closed set it gates on), reading no contract. Its `owns.components[]` declares `mobile/src/components/paywall/SubscriptionLoadingGuard.tsx`.

###### `S-051` `web_subscribe`

**Programme.** `S-051` · scope `platform_shared` · feature `F12` · build order 3123 · batch **UNRESEARCHED** · review `unreviewed` — The subscription and Stripe hand-off, which resolves an entitlement per PRODUCT — so it serves both and belongs to neither.

**What it is.** The hand-off page between the mobile app and the payment provider. A user who taps subscribe in the app arrives here with a one-time code in the web address and no web login; the page trades that code for a payment page and sends the browser straight on to it, showing only a spinner while it works. If the code is missing, already used, or older than fifteen minutes, it shows one honest message telling the user to go back to the app and start again.

**What it reads and writes.** It reads nothing from the database directly. Every value arrives through one contract: `/api/subscribe/exchange`. Behind that contract, the data comes from `logic_variables` and `user_profiles`, and writes land on `subscribe_nonces` and `user_profiles`.

**Under Spec 126.** **REBUILD** — it drives writes, so a client decision has to be re-homed on the server before the projection can be honest. It renders through the WIZARD_STEP renderer (declared step index, advance condition, resume key and skip rule), reading by reference: `/api/subscribe/exchange`. It owns no component of its own, so its `owns.components[]` is an empty array — a legal answer, written down.

###### `S-052` `web_subscribe_cancel`

**Programme.** `S-052` · scope `platform_shared` · feature `F12` · build order 3123 · batch **UNRESEARCHED** · review `unreviewed` — The subscription and Stripe hand-off, which resolves an entitlement per PRODUCT — so it serves both and belongs to neither.

**What it is.** Where the payment provider sends the user if they back out of paying. It is a single reassuring message: no charge was made, and to try again they should return to the mobile app and tap the subscribe link. It fetches nothing and changes nothing.

**What it reads and writes.** This surface reaches **no API contract at all** — every value it shows is local, passed in as a prop, or read from the device.

**Under Spec 126.** **RE-PROJECT** — it writes nothing and holds no Layer-3 store, so the move is short — the server already assembles the payload and only the rendering is client-side. It renders through the STATIC renderer (content source and SEO, or a declared redirect alone), reading no contract. It owns no component of its own, so its `owns.components[]` is an empty array — a legal answer, written down.

###### `S-053` `web_subscribe_success`

**Programme.** `S-053` · scope `platform_shared` · feature `F12` · build order 3123 · batch **UNRESEARCHED** · review `unreviewed` — The subscription and Stripe hand-off, which resolves an entitlement per PRODUCT — so it serves both and belongs to neither.

**What it is.** Where the payment provider sends the user after a successful payment. It confirms the payment was received, then checks the account a few times over about twelve seconds to see whether the upgrade has landed. If it has, it says so; if the check cannot run (the mobile hand-off visitor has no web login) or the upgrade has not appeared yet, it says the account will be active shortly and to return to the app. It never claims the account is active before the server confirms it, and never claims failure.

**What it reads and writes.** It reads nothing from the database directly. Every value arrives through one contract: `/api/user-profile`. Behind that contract, the data comes from `entitlements` and `user_profiles`, and writes land on `entitlements` and `user_profiles`.

**Under Spec 126.** **REBUILD** — it drives writes, so a client decision has to be re-homed on the server before the projection can be honest. It renders through the WIZARD_STEP renderer (declared step index, advance condition, resume key and skip rule), reading by reference: `/api/user-profile`. It owns no component of its own, so its `owns.components[]` is an empty array — a legal answer, written down.

> ⚠️ Bounded poll: 6 attempts x 2s. A 401 on the first poll (the sessionless mobile hand-off case) stops polling immediately and shows the 'pending' copy. /api/user-profile is not in PUBLIC_PATHS, PUBLIC_PREFIXES or PUBLIC_EXACT_API_PATHS, so classifyRoute gives it the fail-closed 'authenticated' class - that 401 is by design, not a bug. Activation truth lives in the Stripe webhook; this page only observes. MEASURED 2026-09-15. WIZARD_STEP fields, recorded here because the schema declares no wizard block: step 2 of 2; advances_on = a profile whose subscription_status is in {active, admin_managed}; resume_key = none; skip_when = the first poll returns 401 (the sessionless mobile-handoff visitor, for whom the app is the confirmation surface per Spec 96 §6); terminal = true. The page is anon-reachable but polls an authenticated contract on purpose — the 401 is a designed branch, not a defect, which is why the auth_class_parity check is written as "the 401 arm must stop immediately" rather than as a mismatch to fix.

###### `C-006` `contract_admin_notifications`

**Programme.** `C-006` · scope `platform_shared` · feature `F13` · build order 3132 · batch **UNRESEARCHED** · review `unreviewed` — Notifications: one device-token registry and one preference set across both products.

**What it is.** Shows an admin the log of push notifications sent to users, newest first and paginated, and — when a specific user is selected — that user's registered devices, notification preferences, and the current on/off switches for the notification system.

**What it reads and writes.** It reads 5 tables — `notification_dispatches`, `notifications`, `device_tokens`, `user_profiles` and `logic_variables` and writes nothing. Its response shape is **unmeasured** as a pick-by-name whitelist — it passes rows through, spreads a row into a computed object, or assembles the payload dynamically, so there is no single list naming what leaves the server. It is called from 2 places: `admin_user_detail`, `admin_notifications`.

**Under Spec 126.** Becomes a **CONTRACT descriptor** of archetype `QUERY`. It declares its `database.reads[]` with named columns, its response projection as an explicit whitelist, its auth class, its rate bucket and its staleness — and `outputs.writes` is forced to `"none"`. Its `consumers[]` becomes the edge list of the fan-out graph — the join nothing in this estate holds today.

###### `C-007` `contract_admin_notifications_test_send`

**Programme.** `C-007` · scope `platform_shared` · feature `F13` · build order 3132 · batch **UNRESEARCHED** · review `unreviewed` — Notifications: one device-token registry and one preference set across both products.

**What it is.** Lets an admin send one real test push notification to a specific device or user to verify the notification pipeline works end to end, without it counting against that user's daily notification limit or appearing in the normal send history.

FINDINGS: (1) DEFECT — malformed JSON returns 502 SEND_FAILED, not 400 (see input_validation above; request.json() at :60 is unguarded). (2) NO AUDIT ROW for a real side effect that reaches a user's device: only a PostHog event (:110-114), no admin_audit_log, and by design no notification_dispatches row (:10-12) — so an operator-sent push is invisible in the DB ledger. (3) An explicit push_token in the body bypasses the device_tokens lookup entirely (:69-70), so an admin can push to ANY Expo token, including one not belonging to any user of this system — there is no ownership check on the supplied token. ###### `C-023` `contract_notifications`

**Programme.** `C-023` · scope `platform_shared` · feature `F13` · build order 3132 · batch **UNRESEARCHED** · review `unreviewed` — Notifications: one device-token registry and one preference set across both products.

**What it is.** Shows a user their own notification inbox, optionally filtered to unread only, and lets them mark one notification or all of their notifications as read.

**What it reads and writes.** It reads 1 table — `notifications` and writes `notifications`. Its response shape is **unmeasured** as a pick-by-name whitelist — it passes rows through, spreads a row into a computed object, or assembles the payload dynamically, so there is no single list naming what leaves the server. **Nothing in this repository calls it.** That is the state this registry exists to make visible, not a claim that it is dead — a caller could be a bookmark, an external system, or a path built from variables.

**Under Spec 126.** Becomes a **CONTRACT descriptor** of archetype `MUTATION`. It declares `database.writes[]` with a `write_discipline` per target (the Spec 122 vocabulary verbatim), its idempotency posture, its optimistic contract and its rollback. Its `consumers[]` is the field that matters most here: today it is empty, and the orphan panel renders that as a red row rather than leaving it to be discovered years later.

###### `C-024` `contract_notifications_preferences`

**Programme.** `C-024` · scope `platform_shared` · feature `F13` · build order 3132 · batch **UNRESEARCHED** · review `unreviewed` — Notifications: one device-token registry and one preference set across both products.

**What it is.** Lets a user see and change their notification settings: which kinds of alerts they receive (new leads above a cost threshold, construction phase changes, stalled jobs, urgent start dates) and what time of day they want them delivered.

**What it reads and writes.** It reads 1 table — `user_profiles` and writes `user_profiles`. Its response is an explicit pick-by-name projection of 5 fields, so a column added to a table upstream does not leak into the client by accident. It is called from 1 place: `mobile_settings`.

**Under Spec 126.** Becomes a **CONTRACT descriptor** of archetype `MUTATION`. It declares `database.writes[]` with a `write_discipline` per target (the Spec 122 vocabulary verbatim), its idempotency posture, its optimistic contract and its rollback. Its `consumers[]` becomes the edge list of the fan-out graph — the join nothing in this estate holds today.

PATCH uses INSERT ... ON CONFLICT (user_id) DO UPDATE so a first-ever PATCH creates the row instead of 404ing — a documented behavioural-parity fix versus the old plain UPDATE. | MEASURED 2026-09-15: CENSUS AGREEMENT: census_reads ['user_profiles'] and census_writes ['user_profiles'] both match. Such a row makes getCurrentUserContext return null (set.length === 0 at src/lib/auth/get-user-context.ts:134-141), so a brand-new user who toggles a notification switch before onboarding gets a profile row that 401s every /api/leads/* route while /api/notifications/preferences keeps working. Second finding: NotificationPrefsSchema is not .strict() (route.ts:24-30) — unknown keys are silently dropped, the opposite of the .strict() convention the leads schemas use (src/features/leads/api/schemas.ts:108). Third: the doc-comment at route.ts:7-9 claims migration 117 flattened these from JSONB; I did NOT verify that against migrations/ — treat it as a claim, not evidence. | Idempotency: Guarded. `INSERT INTO user_profiles (user_id) VALUES ($1) ON CONFLICT (user_id) DO UPDATE SET <only the fields the client sent>, updated_at = NOW()` (route.ts:122-124, SET assembled at :106-115). ###### `S-022` `admin_notifications`

**Programme.** `S-022` · scope `platform_shared` · feature `F13` · build order 3133 · batch **UNRESEARCHED** · review `unreviewed` — Notifications: one device-token registry and one preference set across both products.

**What it is.** The operator's window on push notifications. It lists what was sent, to whom, when and of what type, with device identifiers partly hidden, and lets the operator fire a real test notification to a chosen device and see the delivery receipt. Its `owns.components[]` declares `src/components/admin/NotificationsTool.tsx`.

###### `S-042` `overlay_offline_banner`

**Programme.** `S-042` · scope `platform_shared` · feature `F14` · build order 3143 · batch **UNRESEARCHED** · review `unreviewed` — A cross-cutting overlay that renders over every surface of both products.

**What it is.** A thin amber strip that slides into view at the top of a screen when the phone loses its connection. It tells the user they are offline and how long ago the data they are looking at was last refreshed, which matters when someone is making a real decision from a cached list. When there is no cached data at all it says so instead.

**What it reads and writes.** This surface reaches **no API contract at all** — every value it shows is local, passed in as a prop, or read from the device. It holds no client-side store, so there is no local copy of server state to keep in sync. It emits **no analytics event**, so nothing it does is currently countable.

**Under Spec 126.** **RE-PROJECT** — it writes nothing and holds no Layer-3 store, so the move is short — the server already assembles the payload and only the rendering is client-side. It renders through the STATIC renderer (content source and SEO, or a declared redirect alone), reading no contract. Its `owns.components[]` declares `mobile/src/components/shared/OfflineBanner.tsx`.

###### `S-045` `shell_app_root`

**Programme.** `S-045` · scope `platform_shared` · feature `F14` · build order 3143 · batch **UNRESEARCHED** · review `unreviewed` — A navigation shell. It routes and gates every product surface beneath it — converting it changes both products at once.

**What it is.** The outermost wrapper every screen sits inside. It decides, on each launch, whether to send the user to sign-in, into setup, or into the app proper, based on what the server says about their account. It also catches confirmation links from email, handles incoming push notifications by showing an in-app banner or jumping to the right screen, and offers people whose account is scheduled for deletion a chance to reactivate it.

**What it reads and writes.** It reads nothing from the database directly. Every value arrives through 2 contracts: `/api/user-profile`, `/api/user-profile/reactivate`. Behind those contracts, the data comes from `entitlements`, `logic_variables` and `user_profiles`, and writes land on `entitlements` and `user_profiles`. It also holds client-side state in `authStore`, `notificationStore` and `onboardingStore`, which is the part a server-driven projection has to absorb or justify.

**Under Spec 126.** **REBUILD** — it holds Layer-3 state (`authStore`, `notificationStore` and `onboardingStore`) and drives writes, so a client decision has to be re-homed on the server before the projection can be honest. It renders through the SHELL renderer (declared routing branches, guards and child groups — a shell here is not inert), reading by reference: `/api/user-profile`, `/api/user-profile/reactivate`. Its `owns.components[]` declares `mobile/src/components/shared/NotificationToast.tsx`.

###### `S-049` `shell_web_root`

**Programme.** `S-049` · scope `platform_shared` · feature `F14` · build order 3143 · batch **UNRESEARCHED** · review `unreviewed` — A navigation shell. It routes and gates every product surface beneath it — converting it changes both products at once.

**What it is.** The outermost wrapper every web page renders inside. It sets the browser tab title and description for the whole site and switches on two background services that all pages then share: a cache that remembers fetched data between page visits, and the usage-tracking hookup. It shows nothing of its own - visitors never see it as a page.

**What it reads and writes.** This surface reaches **no API contract at all** — every value it shows is local, passed in as a prop, or read from the device.

**Under Spec 126.** **RE-PROJECT** — it writes nothing and holds no Layer-3 store, so the move is short — the server already assembles the payload and only the rendering is client-side. It renders through the SHELL renderer (declared routing branches, guards and child groups — a shell here is not inert), reading no contract. Its `owns.components[]` declares `src/components/observability/PostHogProvider.tsx`.

###### `C-027` `contract_products`

**Programme.** `C-027` · scope `platform_shared` · feature `F15` · build order 3152 · batch **UNRESEARCHED** · review `unreviewed` — Used by both products and owned by neither.

**What it is.** Returns the fixed list of construction product and material categories the app uses to classify permits, for populating a filter dropdown. No user data or database is involved.

**What it reads and writes.** It touches no table at all. Its response shape is **unmeasured** as a pick-by-name whitelist — it passes rows through, spreads a row into a computed object, or assembles the payload dynamically, so there is no single list naming what leaves the server. **Nothing in this repository calls it.** That is the state this registry exists to make visible, not a claim that it is dead — a caller could be a bookmark, an external system, or a path built from variables.

**Under Spec 126.** Becomes a **CONTRACT descriptor** of archetype `QUERY`. It declares its `database.reads[]` with named columns, its response projection as an explicit whitelist, its auth class, its rate bucket and its staleness — and `outputs.writes` is forced to `"none"`. Its `consumers[]` is the field that matters most here: today it is empty, and the orphan panel renders that as a red row rather than leaving it to be discovered years later.

###### `C-035` `contract_user_profile`

**Programme.** `C-035` · scope `platform_shared` · feature `F15` · build order 3152 · batch **UNRESEARCHED** · review `unreviewed` — Used by both products and owned by neither.

**What it is.** Lets a signed-in user view their own profile and free-trial status — viewing it auto-starts or auto-expires the trial as a side effect — and update profile fields such as name, phone, location, trade and notification preferences. A couple of one-time fields (trade selection, terms acceptance) can only be set once and then lock.

**What it reads and writes.** It reads 2 tables — `user_profiles` and `entitlements` and writes `user_profiles` and `entitlements`. Its response is an explicit pick-by-name projection of 28 fields, so a column added to a table upstream does not leak into the client by accident. It is called from 8 places: `mobile/src/hooks/useUserProfile.ts`, `mobile/src/hooks/usePatchProfile.ts`, `mobile_onboarding_address`, `mobile_onboarding_complete`, `mobile_onboarding_profession`, `mobile_onboarding_supplier`, `mobile_onboarding_terms`, `web_subscribe_success`.

**Under Spec 126.** Becomes a **CONTRACT descriptor** of archetype `MUTATION`. It declares `database.writes[]` with a `write_discipline` per target (the Spec 122 vocabulary verbatim), its idempotency posture, its optimistic contract and its rollback. Its `consumers[]` becomes the edge list of the fan-out graph — the join nothing in this estate holds today.

###### `C-036` `contract_user_profile_delete`

**Programme.** `C-036` · scope `platform_shared` · feature `F15` · build order 3152 · batch **UNRESEARCHED** · review `unreviewed` — Used by both products and owned by neither.

**What it is.** Lets a signed-in user request deletion of their own account. It marks the account and every subscription on it as pending deletion, schedules any active billing to stop at the end of the period they already paid for, and opens a 30-day window during which they can change their mind and reactivate.

**What it reads and writes.** It reads 1 table — `user_profiles` and writes `user_profiles` and `entitlements`. Its response shape is **unmeasured** as a pick-by-name whitelist — it passes rows through, spreads a row into a computed object, or assembles the payload dynamically, so there is no single list naming what leaves the server. **Nothing in this repository calls it.** That is the state this registry exists to make visible, not a claim that it is dead — a caller could be a bookmark, an external system, or a path built from variables.

**Under Spec 126.** Becomes a **CONTRACT descriptor** of archetype `MUTATION`. It declares `database.writes[]` with a `write_discipline` per target (the Spec 122 vocabulary verbatim), its idempotency posture, its optimistic contract and its rollback. Its `consumers[]` is the field that matters most here: today it is empty, and the orphan panel renders that as a red row rather than leaving it to be discovered years later.

###### `S-036` `mobile_settings`

**Programme.** `S-036` · scope `platform_shared` · feature `F15` · build order 3153 · batch **UNRESEARCHED** · review `unreviewed` — User settings write shared `user_profiles` preference columns read by both products.

**What it is.** Where the user reviews their trade, changes how far out they want to see jobs, and chooses which alerts reach them and when. It also tells them if the phone's operating system is blocking notifications and offers a way to fix that, gives paying users a link into the billing portal to cancel or change payment, and holds the sign-out button.

**What it reads and writes.** It reads nothing from the database directly. Every value arrives through 3 contracts: `/api/notifications/preferences`, `/api/user-profile`, `/api/subscribe/portal-session`. Behind those contracts, the data comes from `entitlements` and `user_profiles`, and writes land on `entitlements` and `user_profiles`. It also holds client-side state in `filterStore` and `authStore`, which is the part a server-driven projection has to absorb or justify. It emits **no analytics event**, so nothing it does is currently countable.

**Under Spec 126.** **REBUILD** — it holds Layer-3 state (`filterStore` and `authStore`) and drives writes, so a client decision has to be re-homed on the server before the projection can be honest. It renders through the FORM renderer (every field carrying its Spec 99 §3 ownership row as data, with a declared rollback), reading by reference: `/api/notifications/preferences`, `/api/user-profile`, `/api/subscribe/portal-session`. It owns no component of its own, so its `owns.components[]` is an empty array — a legal answer, written down.

###### `C-003` `contract_admin_app_health`

**Programme.** `C-003` · scope `platform_shared` · feature `F16` · build order 3162 · batch **UNRESEARCHED** · review `unreviewed` — Used by both products and owned by neither.

**What it is.** Powers the admin App Health Dashboard: pulls together five live health signals about the mobile app (crash rate, sign-in success rate, how often people save a lead after viewing one, how often they convert on the paywall, and cache-refresh activity) so the team can see at a glance whether the app is working properly for users.

**What it reads and writes.** It touches no table at all. Its response is an explicit pick-by-name projection of 6 fields, so a column added to a table upstream does not leak into the client by accident. It is called from 1 place: `src/features/admin-app-health/api/useAppHealth.ts`.

**Under Spec 126.** Becomes a **CONTRACT descriptor** of archetype `QUERY`. It declares its `database.reads[]` with named columns, its response projection as an explicit whitelist, its auth class, its rate bucket and its staleness — and `outputs.writes` is forced to `"none"`. Its `consumers[]` becomes the edge list of the fan-out graph — the join nothing in this estate holds today.

###### `C-008` `contract_admin_pipeline_step_output`

**Programme.** `C-008` · scope `platform_shared` · feature `F16` · build order 3162 · batch **UNRESEARCHED** · review `unreviewed` — Used by both products and owned by neither.

**What it is.** Lets an admin browse the raw data rows a single pipeline step actually produced — for example what a parcel-linking run wrote — with optional filtering, so they can inspect and troubleshoot pipeline output directly in the admin UI.

It declares its `database.reads[]` with named columns, its response projection as an explicit whitelist, its auth class, its rate bucket and its staleness — and `outputs.writes` is forced to `"none"`. Its `consumers[]` becomes the edge list of the fan-out graph — the join nothing in this estate holds today.

**Programme.** `C-010` · scope `platform_shared` · feature `F16` · build order 3162 · batch **UNRESEARCHED** · review `unreviewed` — Used by both products and owned by neither.

Its `consumers[]` is the field that matters most here: today it is empty, and the orphan panel renders that as a red row rather than leaving it to be discovered years later.

> ⚠️ The audit row applies only to DELETE (unenroll), which calls writeAdminAudit for 'mfa_unenrolled'. POST (start enrollment) does NOT write an audit row — the 'mfa_enrolled' event is written by .../mfa/verify instead. GET/POST talk to Supabase Auth's MFA API (listFactors/enroll), not a raw table; admin_backup_codes is the only directly queried table. All three verbs require authMethod === 'session' (403 for admin_key/dev_bypass sentinels). POST projection is {factor_id, qr_code, secret, uri}; DELETE is {unenrolled:true}; the recorded projection is the GET shape. | MEASURED 2026-09-15: FINDINGS. (1) AUDIT ASYMMETRY: only DELETE writes admin_audit_log (:138). GET and POST write none — so starting an enrollment (a security-state-changing operation that mints a TOTP secret, :82-85) leaves no audit row; only the PostHog event at :96 records it, and that is best-effort (src/lib/admin/analytics.ts:112 returns early when POSTHOG_API_KEY is unset). (2) Audit failure is deliberately swallowed at :146-149 with the reason stated at :147; the response is still 200, so the caller cannot distinguish audited from unaudited. This is a documented choice, not an accident. (3) The TOTP `secret` and `qr_code` are returned in the response body at :104-105 — intentional per the header comment at :98-100, but it means the plaintext secret transits the envelope. (4) CENSUS DISAGREEMENT: the census lists census_reads [admin_backup_codes] and census_writes [admin_backup_codes, admin_audit_log] — all confirmed — but MISSES `profiles`, which every request reads through verifyAdminAuth (src/lib/auth/verify-admin.ts:117-120). It also misses the conditional admin_backup_codes SELECT/UPDATE inside the MFA gate (src/lib/admin/backup-codes.ts:116, :127), reachable only when ADMIN_MFA_ENFORCED='true'. (5) The TOTP factors themselves are NOT in this repo's Postgres — they live in Supabase GoTrue, reached via supabase.auth.mfa.* at :56, :82, :127; there is no local table for them. (6) No SELECT *. All SQL is parameterised (src/lib/admin/backup-codes.ts:73, :77, :89, :95). | Caching: none observed — no Cache-Control, revalidate, dynamic or in-process cache in the file. | Other guards / classification: CSRF Origin allowlist on POST and DELETE via src/lib/auth/verify-admin.ts:70-78 (MUTATING_METHODS at :45, isOriginAllowed at :319-338, default-deny at :336). MFA aal2 gate at src/lib/auth/verify-admin.ts:143-173 — INERT unless process.env.ADMIN_MFA_ENFORCED === 'true' (:143); when armed, an x-admin-backup-code header (:156) is accepted as a single-use challenge alternative (:158). | No test file under src/tests/** imports this route.

<a id="c-015"></a>

###### `C-015` `contract_admin_security_mfa_verify`

**Programme.** `C-015` · scope `platform_shared` · feature `F16` · build order 3162 · batch **UNRESEARCHED** · review `unreviewed` — Used by both products and owned by neither.

**What it is.** Completes an admin's two-factor setup by checking the six-digit code from their authenticator app; on success it upgrades their login session to a higher trust level and issues one-time backup codes for use if they lose their device.

**What it reads and writes.** It touches no table at all and writes `admin_backup_codes` and `admin_audit_log`. Its response is an explicit pick-by-name projection of 2 fields, so a column added to a table upstream does not leak into the client by accident. It is called from 1 place: `src/features/admin-security/api/useAdminSecurity.ts`.

**Under Spec 126.** Becomes a **CONTRACT descriptor** of archetype `MUTATION`. It declares `database.writes[]` with a `write_discipline` per target (the Spec 122 vocabulary verbatim), its idempotency posture, its optimistic contract and its rollback. Its `consumers[]` becomes the edge list of the fan-out graph — the join nothing in this estate holds today.

> ⚠️ writeAdminAudit is called for 'mfa_enrolled' after backup codes are issued. Challenge/verify goes through Supabase Auth (GoTrue), not a raw table read. replaceBackupCodes deletes all existing rows for the user and inserts 10 fresh hashed rows in one transaction. An audit-write failure here is deliberately swallowed (logged, not thrown) because the factor is already verified and the codes already stored — a 500 would strand a live enrollment and hide the one-time plaintext codes. Requires authMethod === 'session'. | MEASURED 2026-09-15: FINDINGS. (1) CENSUS DISAGREEMENT: census_reads is [] for this route, but it DOES read — `profiles` on every request through verifyAdminAuth (src/lib/auth/verify-admin.ts:117-120), and `admin_backup_codes` through consumeBackupCode when ADMIN_MFA_ENFORCED='true' (src/lib/admin/backup-codes.ts:116). census_writes [admin_backup_codes, admin_audit_log] is confirmed; the admin_backup_codes write is a DELETE+10×INSERT pair inside one transaction (src/lib/admin/backup-codes.ts:72-81), not a single statement. (2) Audit failure swallowed at :98-103 with the reason stated at :99-101 — deliberate, so a caller cannot tell an audited enrollment from an unaudited one. (3) The 10 PLAINTEXT backup codes are returned in the body at :106 — by design (:83-85), stored only as sha256(salt:code) (src/lib/admin/backup-codes.ts:52-56). (4) NO RATE LIMIT on a 6-digit TOTP verify endpoint (:72-76). Brute-force resistance is entirely delegated to Supabase GoTrue; nothing in this repo throttles :44. Worth a reviewer's attention even though the code path is deliberate. (5) Backup-code hashing uses sha256, not a KDF — src/lib/admin/backup-codes.ts:16-24 argues the case explicitly (64-bit server-generated one-time codes). Comment, not evidence; the code is at :52-56. (6) No SELECT *; all SQL parameterised. | Caching: none observed — no Cache-Control, revalidate, dynamic or in-process cache in the file. | Other guards / classification: CSRF Origin allowlist (POST is a MUTATING_METHOD) via src/lib/auth/verify-admin.ts:45 + :70-78, default-deny at :336. MFA aal2 gate src/lib/auth/verify-admin.ts:143-173, inert unless ADMIN_MFA_ENFORCED='true'. TOTP challenge/verify is done server-side against GoTrue at :63 and :72-76 — the 6-digit code is never compared in this repo. | No test file under src/tests/** imports this route.

<a id="c-016"></a>

###### `C-016` `contract_admin_stats`

**Programme.** `C-016` · scope `platform_shared` · feature `F16` · build order 3162 · batch **UNRESEARCHED** · review `unreviewed` — Used by both products and owned by neither.

**What it is.** Powers the main admin dashboard's overview numbers — how many permits, builders, and committee-of-adjustment applications exist, how many are linked to properties, neighbourhoods and contractor-registry records, and how fresh and healthy each data pipeline currently is — so an admin can see overall system health at a glance.

**What it reads and writes.** It reads 20 tables — `permits`, `entities`, `trades`, `trade_mapping_rules`, `sync_runs`, `notifications`, `permit_parcels`, `coa_applications`, `permit_trades`, `address_points`, `parcels`, `building_footprints`, `parcel_buildings`, `neighbourhoods`, `wsib_registry`, `lead_views`, `pipeline_runs`, `pipeline_schedules`, `information_schema.columns` and `pg_class` and writes `pipeline_runs`. Its response is an explicit pick-by-name projection of 38 fields, so a column added to a table upstream does not leak into the client by accident. It is called from 2 places: `web_dashboard`, `admin_data_quality`.

**Under Spec 126.** Becomes a **CONTRACT descriptor** of archetype `QUERY`. It declares its `database.reads[]` with named columns, its response projection as an explicit whitelist, its auth class, its rate bucket and its staleness — and `outputs.writes` is forced to `"none"`. Its `consumers[]` becomes the edge list of the fan-out graph — the join nothing in this estate holds today.

**kind** CONTRACT · **archetype** `QUERY` · **platforms** `web` · **status** exists · **path** `/api/admin/stats` · **methods** `GET` · **lines** 469 · **shard** `contracts` · **unresearched fields: 2**

**Gate.** auth class **admin** (classifyRoute("/api/admin/stats") returns "admin" (executed 2026-09-15); the handler adds no check of its own, so middleware is the only gate.)

**Called by.** `web_dashboard` · `admin_data_quality`

**Emits.** —

No verifyAdminAuth import. Its pipeline-freshness / chain-alias block duplicates pipelines/status/route.ts almost verbatim. Thirty-plus COUNT queries run in parallel, most wrapped in .catch(() => 0) so a missing table degrades a metric rather than failing the response. | MEASURED 2026-09-15: FINDINGS. (1) MISSING GUARD — the most exposed of my six: no verifyAdminAuth (imports :1-7), yet this route fans out ~38 queries across ~20 tables AND performs a WRITE (the reaper at :189). src/lib/auth/verify-admin.ts:9-11 mandates the call; only the presence-only middleware check (src/middleware.ts:115) stands in front of it. (2) The task brief's premise about the 7 engine_health_* logic variables is WRONG FOR THIS ROUTE: /api/admin/stats reads no logic variables at all (whole-file read; no logic_variables SQL, no resolver import). They are read by src/app/api/quality/route.ts (header :37-38, application :211-212), with names/defaults in src/lib/quality/types.ts:492-515. Their Zod bounds and on_invalid posture are UNRESEARCHED — see engine_health_logic_variables.bounds/on_invalid — because /api/quality is not one of my routes. (3) A WRITE HIDES INSIDE A 'QUERY' ROUTE: reapStaleRunningRows() at :189 UPDATEs pipeline_runs to status='failed' (src/lib/admin/reap-stale-runs.ts:26-28). Its only call site in src/ is this GET, so stale-run reaping happens only when a human loads the admin dashboard; and its failure is swallowed by an empty catch (src/lib/admin/reap-stale-runs.ts:38-40). (4) UNPARAMETERISED SQL INTERPOLATION at :102: `linked_confidence < ${COA_IDENTITY_LINK_MIN_CONFIDENCE}` splices a TS module constant (src/lib/coa/link-confidence.ts:17, value 0.85) straight into the SQL string. Not injectable today (compile-time numeric constant, no request input on this route), but it is the one string-built predicate here. (5) SILENT-DEGRADATION CLASS: 15 `.catch(() => [{count:'0'}])` swallows (:123-186) plus 6 block-level empty catches (:222, :280, :350, :367, :387, :406) mean a broken table renders as a plausible zero with no error signal, no logError, and no flag in the payload. Note the asymmetry — the first ~17 queries (:52-119) have NO .catch, so those failures 500 the whole route. (6) KNOWN GAP, COMMENT vs CODE: the comment block at :296-301 says the 3-status IN-list misses run-chain.js's 4th status 'deferred_to_full'. The CODE is at :317 — `status IN ('completed','completed_with_warnings','completed_with_errors')` — and indeed omits it, so a deferred chain reads as never-completed and therefore stale (:342-344). The comment's claim matches the code, but the comment is not the evidence; :317 is. (7) ENVELOPE DEVIATION: bare 38-key object at :413-461, bare {error} at :464-467 (see envelope.deviations). (8) NO SELECT * on this route. (9) CENSUS AGREES COMPLETELY: all 20 census_reads tables confirmed at the lines above, and census_writes [pipeline_runs] confirmed at :189 -> src/lib/admin/reap-stale-runs.ts:26. <a id="c-017"></a>

###### `C-017` `contract_admin_sync`

**Programme.** `C-017` · scope `platform_shared` · feature `F16` · build order 3162 · batch **UNRESEARCHED** · review `unreviewed` — Used by both products and owned by neither.

**What it is.** Shows an admin the history of the last twenty permit-data import runs, and lets them manually trigger a new import of permit data from a file already sitting on the server.

**What it reads and writes.** It reads 5 tables — `sync_runs`, `trade_mapping_rules`, `trades`, `permit_type_classifications` and `permits` and writes `sync_runs`, `permits`, `permit_trades` and `permit_history`. Its response is an explicit pick-by-name projection of 12 fields, so a column added to a table upstream does not leak into the client by accident. **Nothing in this repository calls it.** That is the state this registry exists to make visible, not a claim that it is dead — a caller could be a bookmark, an external system, or a path built from variables. It mutates admin state and writes **no `admin_audit_log` row** — one of the nine measured gaps Phase 0 closes.

**Under Spec 126.** Becomes a **CONTRACT descriptor** of archetype `COMMAND`. It declares the JOB it triggers (`job_ref`), its concurrency posture and the audit row it must write. Its `consumers[]` is the field that matters most here: today it is empty, and the orphan panel renders that as a red row rather than leaving it to be discovered years later.

###### `C-018` `contract_admin_users`

**Programme.** `C-018` · scope `platform_shared` · feature `F16` · build order 3162 · batch **UNRESEARCHED** · review `unreviewed` — Used by both products and owned by neither.

**What it is.** Gives an admin a searchable, filterable, paginated directory of all user accounts, and lets an admin manually create a new supplier or enterprise account — creating their login, sending a password-reset link and setting up their profile — for accounts that are not self-service signups.

**What it reads and writes.** It reads 2 tables — `user_profiles` and `entitlements` and writes `user_profiles`, `entitlements` and `admin_audit_log`. Its response shape is **unmeasured** as a pick-by-name whitelist — it passes rows through, spreads a row into a computed object, or assembles the payload dynamically, so there is no single list naming what leaves the server. It is called from 1 place: `src/features/admin-users/api/useAdminUsers.ts`.

**Under Spec 126.** Becomes a **CONTRACT descriptor** of archetype `MUTATION`. It declares `database.writes[]` with a `write_discipline` per target (the Spec 122 vocabulary verbatim), its idempotency posture, its optimistic contract and its rollback. Its `consumers[]` becomes the edge list of the fan-out graph — the join nothing in this estate holds today.

<a id="c-019"></a>

###### `C-019` `contract_admin_users_uid`

**Programme.** `C-019` · scope `platform_shared` · feature `F16` · build order 3162 · batch **UNRESEARCHED** · review `unreviewed` — Used by both products and owned by neither.

**What it is.** Lets an admin look up one user's full account record and activity, and make account-level changes to it: change which trades they're assigned, change their account tier, extend a free trial, revoke or suspend access, or permanently delete the account including cancelling their billing and scrubbing their personal data.

**What it reads and writes.** It reads 4 tables — `user_profiles`, `entitlements`, `lead_views` and `lead_view_events` and writes `user_profiles`, `entitlements` and `admin_audit_log`. Its response is an explicit pick-by-name projection of 20 fields, so a column added to a table upstream does not leak into the client by accident. It is called from 1 place: `src/features/admin-users/api/useAdminUsers.ts`.

**Under Spec 126.** Becomes a **CONTRACT descriptor** of archetype `MUTATION`. It declares `database.writes[]` with a `write_discipline` per target (the Spec 122 vocabulary verbatim), its idempotency posture, its optimistic contract and its rollback. Its `consumers[]` becomes the edge list of the fan-out graph — the join nothing in this estate holds today.

###### `C-028` `contract_quality`

**Programme.** `C-028` · scope `platform_shared` · feature `F16` · build order 3162 · batch **UNRESEARCHED** · review `unreviewed` — Used by both products and owned by neither.

**What it is.** Returns the current data-quality dashboard and its 30-day trend: permit, trade, property and committee-of-adjustment metrics, detected volume, schema and duration anomalies, recent pipeline failures, and live database health statistics — for staff monitoring system health.

**What it reads and writes.** It reads 4 tables — `data_quality_snapshots`, `pipeline_runs`, `logic_variables` and `pg_stat_user_tables` and writes nothing. Its response shape is **unmeasured** as a pick-by-name whitelist — it passes rows through, spreads a row into a computed object, or assembles the payload dynamically, so there is no single list naming what leaves the server. It is called from 1 place: `admin_data_quality`.

**Under Spec 126.** Becomes a **CONTRACT descriptor** of archetype `QUERY`. It declares its `database.reads[]` with named columns, its response projection as an explicit whitelist, its auth class, its rate bucket and its staleness — and `outputs.writes` is forced to `"none"`. Its `consumers[]` becomes the edge list of the fan-out graph — the join nothing in this estate holds today.

###### `C-029` `contract_quality_refresh`

**Programme.** `C-029` · scope `platform_shared` · feature `F16` · build order 3162 · batch **UNRESEARCHED** · review `unreviewed` — Used by both products and owned by neither.

**What it is.** Forces an immediate recomputation of today's data-quality snapshot — permit counts, trade-match rates, builder enrichment, property linkage and so on — instead of waiting for the next scheduled capture, so the quality dashboard reflects current numbers on demand.

**What it reads and writes.** It reads 9 tables — `permits`, `permit_trades`, `entities`, `permit_parcels`, `coa_applications`, `building_footprints`, `parcel_buildings`, `permit_inspections` and `sync_runs` and writes `data_quality_snapshots`. Its response shape is **unmeasured** as a pick-by-name whitelist — it passes rows through, spreads a row into a computed object, or assembles the payload dynamically, so there is no single list naming what leaves the server. **Nothing in this repository calls it.** That is the state this registry exists to make visible, not a claim that it is dead — a caller could be a bookmark, an external system, or a path built from variables.

**Under Spec 126.** Becomes a **CONTRACT descriptor** of archetype `COMMAND`. It declares the JOB it triggers (`job_ref`), its concurrency posture and the audit row it must write. Its `consumers[]` is the field that matters most here: today it is empty, and the orphan panel renders that as a red row rather than leaving it to be discovered years later.

A 20-line handler whose entire body delegates to captureDataQualitySnapshot() in src/lib/quality/metrics.ts, which fans out roughly sixteen parallel counting queries across the listed tables and upserts one row per day into data_quality_snapshots (ON CONFLICT (snapshot_date) DO UPDATE). No in-repo caller found. | MEASURED 2026-09-15: THE CLASSIFICATION QUESTION (both line numbers): '/api/quality/refresh' appears in AUTHENTICATED_API_ROUTES at src/lib/auth/route-guard.ts:122 and '/api/quality' appears in PUBLIC_PREFIXES at src/lib/auth/route-guard.ts:75. classifyRoute tests AUTHENTICATED_API_ROUTES FIRST at route-guard.ts:165 and returns at :166; the PUBLIC_PREFIXES test is at :170. Because :166 returns, :170 is unreachable for this path — AUTHENTICATED WINS. So this route is NOT public, despite the task brief's premise. Consequence a reviewer must know: the handler carries NO in-handler auth (route.ts:9 takes no request and calls no guard), so authentication rests ENTIRELY on middleware ordering. If someone ever reorders those two branches, or adds a sibling like /api/quality/refresh-all (which would match only the public prefix), this write endpoint silently becomes anonymous. It is also UNAUTHENTICATED-EQUIVALENT in dev: src/middleware.ts:49-77 short-circuits every non-public route when isDevMode() (src/lib/auth/route-guard.ts:33). Second finding: it is an unrestricted work trigger — any authenticated user (no admin check, no rate limit) can fire 16 parallel full-table aggregate queries (src/lib/quality/metrics.ts:25-42, Promise.all over COUNT(*)-class scans of permits/permit_trades/entities/coa_applications/permit_parcels/permit_inspections) and overwrite today's data_quality_snapshots row. The write is idempotent per day (ON CONFLICT (snapshot_date) DO UPDATE, metrics.ts:167) so it is not destructive across days, but it does let a non-admin rewrite the row /api/quality then serves publicly. CHECKLIST agreement: routes-index.json census_reads listed 9 tables (permits, permit_trades, entities, permit_parcels, coa_applications, building_footprints, parcel_buildings, permit_inspections, sync_runs) — all 9 confirmed, and I found ONE MORE the checklist omits: information_schema.columns (src/lib/quality/metrics.ts:642-648, feeding schema_column_counts). census_writes [data_quality_snapshots] confirmed exactly. | Caching: none observed — no revalidate/dynamic export and no Cache-Control header in src/app/api/quality/refresh/route.ts:1-20 (a POST route is not cached by default in any case) | Other guards / classification: CLASSIFICATION VERDICT: 'authenticated' WINS. Two branches match this exact path and the ORDER decides it. (1) AUTHENTICATED_API_ROUTES contains the exact string '/api/quality/refresh' (src/lib/auth/route-guard.ts:122) and is tested at route-guard.ts:165 — `pathname === r` is true, so classifyRoute RETURNS 'authenticated' at route-guard.ts:166. (2) PUBLIC_PREFIXES contains '/api/quality' (route-guard.ts:75) and is tested at route-guard.ts:170 — `startsWith` would also be true, but line 170 is NEVER REACHED for this path because line 166 already returned. So /api/quality/refresh is AUTHENTICATED while its sibling /api/quality (which matches only the prefix branch) is PUBLIC. | ORPHAN — zero call sites in src/** or mobile/** (sweep 2026-09-15, comment lines stripped). | No test file under src/tests/** imports this route.

###### `C-033` `contract_sync`

**Programme.** `C-033` · scope `platform_shared` · feature `F16` · build order 3162 · batch **UNRESEARCHED** · review `unreviewed` — Used by both products and owned by neither.

**What it is.** Shows the history of recent data-import runs that pull the City of Toronto's open permit data into the system, and lets an operator manually kick off a new import from a given file, updating and classifying permits as it goes.

**What it reads and writes.** It reads 5 tables — `sync_runs`, `trade_mapping_rules`, `trades`, `permit_type_classifications` and `permits` and writes `sync_runs`, `permits`, `permit_trades` and `permit_history`. Its response shape is **unmeasured** as a pick-by-name whitelist — it passes rows through, spreads a row into a computed object, or assembles the payload dynamically, so there is no single list naming what leaves the server. **Nothing in this repository calls it.** That is the state this registry exists to make visible, not a claim that it is dead — a caller could be a bookmark, an external system, or a path built from variables.

**Under Spec 126.** Becomes a **CONTRACT descriptor** of archetype `COMMAND`. It declares the JOB it triggers (`job_ref`), its concurrency posture and the audit row it must write. Its `consumers[]` is the field that matters most here: today it is empty, and the orphan panel renders that as a red row rather than leaving it to be discovered years later.

> ⚠️ No SPEC LINK header. POST dynamically imports src/lib/sync/process.ts (runSync) to avoid loading the sync machinery on every request. runSync processes each permit record in its own transaction so one bad record does not roll back the batch. Classified COMMAND because the endpoint's stated job is to trigger a sync run, though GET alone would be QUERY. No in-repo caller found. | MEASURED 2026-09-15: WHAT IT HONESTLY IS: a 53-line thin wrapper. GET is a raw `SELECT * FROM sync_runs ORDER BY started_at DESC LIMIT 20` returned unprojected (:11-15). POST takes `{ file_path }`, dynamically imports `runSync` from src/lib/sync/process.ts (:42) and returns the finished sync_runs row. All real work — the 9 write statements and 5 reads enumerated above — lives in src/lib/sync/process.ts (404 lines, read in full). RISK a reviewer must know: POST performs a mass DB mutation across permits / permit_trades / permit_history with NO in-handler auth check and NO validation of file_path beyond truthiness (:32-39); the only gate is the middleware presence-check, which middleware.ts:84-89 itself documents as non-cryptographic. CENSUS AGREEMENT: the routes-index read/write table matches exactly. | Idempotency: NOT GUARDED at the route level. Every POST unconditionally INSERTs a new sync_runs row (src/lib/sync/process.ts:322-326) — there is no in-flight lock, advisory lock, dedup key or ON CONFLICT anywhere in the run lifecycle, so two concurrent or repeated POSTs with the same file_path start two concurrent full syncs. Downstream, the per-permit work is partially convergent: an unchanged content hash short-circuits to a last_seen_at touch (process.ts:209, :282-288) and permit_trades are DELETEd before re-INSERT (process.ts:261-264), but permit_history rows accumulate one set per run that observes a diff (process.ts:248-257), and sync_runs rows accumulate unconditionally. | Caching: none observed — no Cache-Control header, no revalidate/dynamic export (full file read :1-53) | ORPHAN — zero call sites in src/** or mobile/** (sweep 2026-09-15, comment lines stripped). | No test file under src/tests/** imports this route.

###### `S-018` `admin_app_health`

**Programme.** `S-018` · scope `platform_shared` · feature `F16` · build order 3163 · batch **UNRESEARCHED** · review `unreviewed` — An admin surface that operates the PLATFORM (users, entitlements, security, tunables, pipeline health) rather than either product specifically.

**What it is.** An operator's at-a-glance read on how the mobile and web apps are behaving. Five tiles show the crash rate over the last day, how many sign-in attempts succeed by method over the last week, how often a viewed lead gets saved, how often the paywall gets clicked, and how much cache-refresh chatter there was. Each tile links out to the deeper analytics tools, and a tile that cannot reach its data source says so with the reason instead of showing a wrong number.

**What it reads and writes.** It reads nothing from the database directly. Every value arrives through one contract: `/api/admin/app-health`. Those contracts' own table reads are recorded on their rows.

**Under Spec 126.** **RE-PROJECT** — it writes nothing and holds no Layer-3 store, so the move is short — the server already assembles the payload and only the rendering is client-side. It renders through the DASHBOARD renderer (tiles that each declare their own contract and degrade independently), reading by reference: `/api/admin/app-health`. Its `owns.components[]` declares `src/components/admin/HealthTile.tsx`.

###### `S-019` `admin_control_panel`

**Programme.** `S-019` · scope `platform_shared` · feature `F16` · build order 3163 · batch **UNRESEARCHED** · review `unreviewed` — An admin surface that operates the PLATFORM (users, entitlements, security, tunables, pipeline health) rather than either product specifically.

**What it is.** Where an operator edits the tuning numbers the pipeline runs on - the platform-wide variables, the per-trade multipliers, and the scope-intensity grid - across three tabs. Edits are held as a draft until the operator presses apply, at which point a dialog shows exactly what is about to change; confirming saves the new values and then kicks off the downstream re-calculation.

**What it reads and writes.** It reads nothing from the database directly. Every value arrives through 2 contracts: `/api/admin/control-panel/configs`, `/api/admin/control-panel/resync`. Behind those contracts, the data comes from `logic_variables`, `scope_intensity_matrix`, `trade_configurations` and `trade_sqft_rates`, and writes land on `logic_variables`, `scope_intensity_matrix`, `trade_configurations` and `trade_sqft_rates`.

**Under Spec 126.** **REBUILD** — it drives writes, so a client decision has to be re-homed on the server before the projection can be honest. It renders through the FORM renderer (every field carrying its Spec 99 §3 ownership row as data, with a declared rollback), reading by reference: `/api/admin/control-panel/configs`, `/api/admin/control-panel/resync`. It owns no component of its own, so its `owns.components[]` is an empty array — a legal answer, written down.

<a id="s-020"></a>

###### `S-020` `admin_data_quality`

**Programme.** `S-020` · scope `platform_shared` · feature `F16` · build order 3163 · batch **UNRESEARCHED** · review `unreviewed` — An admin surface that operates the PLATFORM (users, entitlements, security, tunables, pipeline health) rather than either product specifically.

**What it is.** The operator's view of how healthy the data itself is: how much of each source has been matched, how confident those matches are, how fresh each feed is against its target schedule, and where records drop out of the funnel between stages. It also lists every pipeline job with its last run, lets the operator start or stop a job and edit its schedule, and offers a timeline per job with its recent run history.

**What it reads and writes.** It reads nothing from the database directly. Every value arrives through 6 contracts: `/api/quality`, `/api/admin/stats`, `/api/admin/pipelines/status`, `/api/admin/pipelines/[slug]`, `/api/admin/pipelines/schedules`, `/api/admin/pipelines/history`. Behind those contracts, the data comes from `address_points`, `building_footprints`, `coa_applications`, `data_quality_snapshots`, `entities`, `information_schema.columns`, `lead_views`, `logic_variables`, `neighbourhoods`, `notifications`, `parcel_buildings`, `parcels`, `permit_parcels`, `permit_trades`, `permits`, `pg_class`, `pg_stat_user_tables`, `pipeline_runs`, `pipeline_schedules`, `sync_runs`, `trade_mapping_rules`, `trades` and `wsib_registry`, and writes land on `pipeline_runs` and `pipeline_schedules`.

**Under Spec 126.** **REBUILD** — it drives writes, so a client decision has to be re-homed on the server before the projection can be honest. It renders through the DASHBOARD renderer (tiles that each declare their own contract and degrade independently), reading by reference: `/api/quality`, `/api/admin/stats`, `/api/admin/pipelines/status`, `/api/admin/pipelines/[slug]`, `/api/admin/pipelines/schedules`, `/api/admin/pipelines/history`. Its `owns.components[]` declares `src/components/DataQualityDashboard.tsx`, `src/components/FreshnessTimeline.tsx`, `src/components/funnel/FunnelPanels.tsx` and `src/components/ScheduleEditModal.tsx`.

**kind** SURFACE · **archetype** `DASHBOARD` · **platforms** `web` · **status** exists · **lines** 2482 · **shard** `admin-existing` · **unresearched fields: 6**

**Gate.** auth class **admin** (The page is behind the /admin/* arm, but four of its six contracts never call verifyAdminAuth and one of them, /api/quality, is deliberately PUBLIC — an admin-gated page mixing a public contract with admin ones.) · session **admin** (classifyRoute('/admin/data-quality') matches the admin-pages arm via `pathname.startsWith('/admin/')` -> 'admin'.)

**Calls.** `/api/quality` · `/api/admin/stats` · `/api/admin/pipelines/status` · `/api/admin/pipelines/[slug]` · `/api/admin/pipelines/schedules` · `/api/admin/pipelines/history`

**Components owned.** `src/components/DataQualityDashboard.tsx` · `src/components/FreshnessTimeline.tsx` · `src/components/funnel/FunnelPanels.tsx` · `src/components/ScheduleEditModal.tsx`

**Emits.** —

**Render states seen in code.** `loading` · `error` · `loaded`

###### `S-021` `admin_home`

**Programme.** `S-021` · scope `platform_shared` · feature `F16` · build order 3163 · batch **UNRESEARCHED** · review `unreviewed` — An admin surface that operates the PLATFORM (users, entitlements, security, tunables, pipeline health) rather than either product specifically.

**What it is.** The operator's front page: a grid of ten tiles, each a doorway to one internal tool - data quality, market metrics, lead-feed testing, the parcel cost model, the flight centre watchlist, the configuration control panel, app health, user management, notifications, and security. It is navigation only; it loads no data of its own and shows no numbers.

**What it reads and writes.** This surface reaches **no API contract at all** — every value it shows is local, passed in as a prop, or read from the device.

**Under Spec 126.** **RE-PROJECT** — it writes nothing and holds no Layer-3 store, so the move is short — the server already assembles the payload and only the rendering is client-side. It renders through the STATIC renderer (content source and SEO, or a declared redirect alone), reading no contract. It owns no component of its own, so its `owns.components[]` is an empty array — a legal answer, written down.

**kind** SURFACE · **archetype** `STATIC` · **platforms** `web` · **status** exists · **lines** 165 · **shard** `admin-existing` · **unresearched fields: 3**

<a id="s-023"></a>

###### `S-023` `admin_pipeline_step_output`

**Programme.** `S-023` · scope `platform_shared` · feature `F16` · build order 3163 · batch **UNRESEARCHED** · review `unreviewed` — An admin surface that operates the PLATFORM (users, entitlements, security, tunables, pipeline health) rather than either product specifically.

**What it is.** A plain row browser over whatever table a chosen pipeline step writes to. The operator arrives with a step already selected (usually from the freshness timeline's inspect link), pages through the rows fifty at a time, and can narrow them by typing a field name and value then pressing apply. Rows that carry a permit identity link straight through to the per-record inspector. It is read-only.

**What it reads and writes.** It reads nothing from the database directly. Every value arrives through one contract: `/api/admin/pipeline/step-output`. Behind that contract, the data comes from `information_schema.columns` and `pg_class`.

###### `S-024` `admin_security`

**Programme.** `S-024` · scope `platform_shared` · feature `F16` · build order 3163 · batch **UNRESEARCHED** · review `unreviewed` — An admin surface that operates the PLATFORM (users, entitlements, security, tunables, pipeline health) rather than either product specifically.

**What it is.** Where an administrator turns on two-factor sign-in for their own account. It shows whether a authenticator app is already registered, walks through adding one by displaying a setup code to scan and asking for the six digits back to prove it worked, and then shows a set of one-time backup codes. The setup code and the backup codes are shown exactly once - leaving the screen loses them for good. It also allows removing a registered device behind a confirmation.

**What it reads and writes.** It reads nothing from the database directly. Every value arrives through 2 contracts: `/api/admin/security/mfa`, `/api/admin/security/mfa/verify`. Behind those contracts, the data comes from `admin_backup_codes`, and writes land on `admin_audit_log` and `admin_backup_codes`.

**Under Spec 126.** **REBUILD** — it drives writes, so a client decision has to be re-homed on the server before the projection can be honest. It renders through the FORM renderer (every field carrying its Spec 99 §3 ownership row as data, with a declared rollback), reading by reference: `/api/admin/security/mfa`, `/api/admin/security/mfa/verify`. It owns no component of its own, so its `owns.components[]` is an empty array — a legal answer, written down.

###### `S-025` `admin_user_detail`

**Programme.** `S-025` · scope `platform_shared` · feature `F16` · build order 3163 · batch **UNRESEARCHED** · review `unreviewed` — An admin surface that operates the PLATFORM (users, entitlements, security, tunables, pipeline health) rather than either product specifically.

**What it is.** One account, in full, with the controls to change it. Cards cover the profile, the subscription (including tools to compare the stored status against the payment provider, apply a correction, retry a failed cancellation, and view recent payment events), the persona-and-trades assignment, and a read-only summary of the account's notification devices, preferences and last message sent. Every change requires the operator to type a reason, and destructive ones go through a confirmation dialog. A banner warns when the account is inside its thirty-day deletion window and records that the operator looked.

**What it reads and writes.** It reads nothing from the database directly. Every value arrives through 5 contracts: `/api/admin/users/[uid]`, `/api/admin/users/[uid]/subscription/reconcile`, `/api/admin/users/[uid]/subscription/retry-cancel`, `/api/admin/users/[uid]/subscription/events`, `/api/admin/notifications`. Behind those contracts, the data comes from `device_tokens`, `entitlements`, `lead_view_events`, `lead_views`, `logic_variables`, `notification_dispatches`, `notifications`, `stripe_webhook_events` and `user_profiles`, and writes land on `admin_audit_log`, `entitlements` and `user_profiles`.

**Under Spec 126.** **REBUILD** — it drives writes, so a client decision has to be re-homed on the server before the projection can be honest. It renders through the DETAIL renderer (one entity, a single-param query key, declared sections), reading by reference: `/api/admin/users/[uid]`, `/api/admin/users/[uid]/subscription/reconcile`, `/api/admin/users/[uid]/subscription/retry-cancel`, `/api/admin/users/[uid]/subscription/events`, `/api/admin/notifications`. Its `owns.components[]` declares `src/components/admin/NotificationsCard.tsx`.

<a id="s-026"></a>

###### `S-026` `admin_users`

**Programme.** `S-026` · scope `platform_shared` · feature `F16` · build order 3163 · batch **UNRESEARCHED** · review `unreviewed` — An admin surface that operates the PLATFORM (users, entitlements, security, tunables, pipeline health) rather than either product specifically.

**What it is.** The operator's directory of every account. It searches by email, phone, name or company and filters by account persona, subscription status, trade, and whether a subscription cancellation failed at the payment provider. Results are paged by the server, and each row opens that account's detail page. A button opens a small form for creating a supplier or enterprise account directly.

**What it reads and writes.** It reads nothing from the database directly. Every value arrives through one contract: `/api/admin/users`. Behind that contract, the data comes from `entitlements` and `user_profiles`, and writes land on `admin_audit_log`, `entitlements` and `user_profiles`.

**Under Spec 126.** **REBUILD** — it drives writes, so a client decision has to be re-homed on the server before the projection can be honest. It renders through the LIST renderer (a collection with declared pagination, recycling and empty/offline states), reading by reference: `/api/admin/users`. It owns no component of its own, so its `owns.components[]` is an empty array — a legal answer, written down.

Both handlers verify on their first line and POST additionally refuses the x-admin-key credential, so an account cannot be provisioned by a CI token.) · session **admin** (classifyRoute('/admin/users') matches the admin-pages arm via `pathname.startsWith('/admin/')` -> 'admin'.)

###### `S-050` `web_login`

**Programme.** `S-050` · scope `platform_shared` · feature `F16` · build order 3163 · batch **UNRESEARCHED** · review `unreviewed` — Used by both products and owned by neither.

**What it is.** Where a visitor signs in or creates an account. It offers email-and-password sign-in, a sign-up form that also collects a name and whether the account is an individual or a company, and a Google sign-in button. Administrators with two-factor turned on get a second box asking for the six-digit code from their authenticator app. When the visitor was bounced here from a page that needed a login, it sends them back to that page afterwards, and only to pages on this site.

**What it reads and writes.** This surface reaches **no API contract at all** — every value it shows is local, passed in as a prop, or read from the device.

**Under Spec 126.** **RE-PROJECT** — it writes nothing and holds no Layer-3 store, so the move is short — the server already assembles the payload and only the rendering is client-side. It renders through the GATE renderer (a `statuses_handled[]` that must cover every value of the closed set it gates on), reading no contract. Its `owns.components[]` declares `src/components/auth/LoginForm.tsx`.

**kind** SURFACE · **archetype** `GATE` · **platforms** `web` · **status** exists · **lines** 407 · **shard** `web-product` · **unresearched fields: 3**

**Gate.** auth class **anon** (`/login` is in PUBLIC_PATHS and the lock pins classifyRoute('/login') === 'public'; a signed-in visitor is never bounced away from it.) · session **public** (classifyRoute('/login') reaches the PUBLIC_PATHS exact-list arm - '/login' is the second entry - and returns 'public'. No earlier arm matches ('/login' is not a PUBLIC_FILE, not under /_next/ or /api/, not '/admin' or '/admin/...', and no PUBLIC_PREFIXES entry is a prefix of it).)

The 'Continue as Dev' button renders only when NEXT_PUBLIC_DEV_MODE=true; the middleware's real bypass reads the server-only DEV_MODE AND NODE_ENV!=='production' (route-guard.ts isDevMode), so the button is cosmetic. Redirect target is guarded by safeRedirectPath (rejects absolute, protocol-relative and backslash forms). MEASURED 2026-09-15: the page holds TWO independently-gated views (credential form and TOTP challenge) but they are one component and one route, so R-13 keeps them one surface rather than promoting the challenge. guards.flag records NEXT_PUBLIC_DEV_MODE because it is what THIS page reads (login/page.tsx:7); the security-bearing flag is the server-only DEV_MODE + NODE_ENV pair in route-guard.ts:32-34 — the two are deliberately different vars and the disagreement is the point, not a defect. a11y.touch_target_min_px stays UNRESEARCHED: the submit buttons measure px-4 py-2.5 on text-sm = 40px, which the vocabulary (UNRESEARCHED or an integer >= 44) cannot express.

### §D `estate_other` — the OTHER product — inventory and seam only (46)

**Not governed by this programme.** Lead generation, the flight center, the lead feed, permit and job detail, builders and entities. Spec 100 §1 fences the parcel tool off from these (*"not coupled to the Lead Feed, Flight Center, or LeadDetail"*), and Spec 128 **R-03** keeps that fence. They appear here for one reason: so a contract shared with scope C, or a contract with no caller at all, is **visible** rather than hidden. They convert under the same standard in a later programme.

## 6. Glossary

| Term | Meaning |
|---|---|
| **Surface** | One thing that renders — a mobile screen, a web page, an admin tool, an overlay, a navigation shell. The unit this standard is built around. |
| **Contract** | One API endpoint: its request, its response projection, the tables it touches, its auth class, and the surfaces that call it. A separate unit from the surface, because one contract commonly serves several. |
| **Job** | Server work with no screen and no request — a scheduled database task or a workflow that runs on a timer. |
| **Archetype** | The *kind* of a surface, contract or job, which determines **which descriptor fields are mandatory**. Not a renderer label (§0.5). |
| **Descriptor** | The machine-readable declaration of one surface, contract or job — 21 categories, answered from a closed menu, validated before anything runs. The contract of the whole standard. |
| **Projection** | The server-assembled shape a surface renders. One payload can have several projections (web, mobile, admin, PDF) without being declared more than once. |
| **Ledger** | An append-only record of things that happened — a usage event, a pipeline run, an admin action. Counters are derived from it by counting rows, never stored alongside it. |
| **Gate** | What must be true before a surface renders or a contract answers: a session, an entitlement product, a feature flag, a device permission, a role. |
| **Golden** | A captured artifact that pins behaviour — here a **pair**: the API response fixture, and the rendered tree produced from it. A change that alters either shows up as a diff. |
| **Drift lock** | A test that regenerates a generated artifact and fails if the committed copy differs. It is what makes "generated, do not hand-edit" true rather than aspirational. |
| **RE-PROJECT / REBUILD** | Whether a surface can be re-rendered from a server projection as-is, or first needs a client-side decision re-homed on the server (§0.8). |
| **Orphan** | A contract with no caller, or a surface with no contract. Both are rendered, because the join between them is the thing nothing in this estate has held. |
